skytree.facts: 634 meters high · Opened in 2012 · The world’s tallest self-standing radio tower
skytree.hist: Completed and opened in 2012, it is a new tower built to solve the problem of radio wave obstruction caused by the increase in high-rise buildings in Tokyo. The height of 634 meters is taken from the homophony of Tokyo's old country name "Musashi" (む・さ・し = 6・3・4). In 2011, it was recognized by the Guinness Book of World Records as the world's tallest tower.
skytree.now: Play: Climb to the 350-meter Tembo Deck and the 450-meter Tembo Corridor for panoramic views. The Sumida Aquarium under the tower is suitable for parents and children, and there is a Pokémon Center in the Skytree City. Eat: The restaurant street on the 6th and 7th floors of Solamachi has the most choices. The famous tsukemen restaurants Rokurisha and Susuen are both here. Buy: Tokyo Skytree City Solamachi has more than 300 stores, and you can buy souvenirs such as Tokyo Banana and limited-edition Skytree merchandise all at once.
skytree.desc: The 634-meter-tall radio tower is characterized by its gradually rounded shape from a triangular base. You can overlook the entire Tokyo from the observatory, and you can see Mount Fuji when the weather is good.
details: Floor guide

From the 4F entrance, take the high-speed elevator for about 50 seconds to reach the 350m Tembo Deck (three floors: 340 glass floor/345 souvenir shop and restaurant/350 circular observation corridor and cafe). 450m Tembo Corridor is a gently ascending glass slope corridor with the highest point 451.2m. Tokyo Skytree City under the tower: Solamachi Mall 1–7F + 30/31F dining floor, Sumida Aquarium is on 5–6F.
Tickets (current price on official website)

Starting from April 2026, the price will fluctuate on a daily basis: the official website booking for Tembo Deck starts from ¥1,800 for adults, and the Tembo Deck + Corridor package starts from ¥3,000 (children are about half price, and those under 5 years old are free); after reaching 350m, you can add the cloister ticket alone for ¥1,400. Special note: There is an additional ¥500 ticketing fee for each ticket purchased at the on-site 4F window or ticket vending machine. Be sure to buy date and time tickets on the official website in advance.
Practical tips

It’s a perfect match with Asakusa: it’s about a 20-minute walk or one train stop away. We recommend the “Asakusa morning session + Skytree evening session” to see both old and new Tokyo. Choose a day that clears up after rain to have the best visibility and a higher probability of seeing Mount Fuji in the morning. The classic spots to take panoramic views of the tower are at the Sumida River Azuma Bridge and the free observation deck on the 8th floor of the Asakusa Culture and Tourism Center.

sensoji.facts: Founded in 628 (legend) · The oldest temple in Tokyo · The Kaminarimon lantern weighs approximately 700 kg
sensoji.hist: Legend has it that in 628, fishermen salvaged the statue of Kannon from the Sumida River, and Sensoji Temple was born. It was officially built in 645. During the Edo period, it became the center of civilian belief and entertainment. The layout of the Kaminarimon and Nakamise shopping streets was basically formed at that time. The main hall and Kaminarimon were damaged in the air raids in World War II, and what you see now is the post-war reconstruction.
sensoji.now: Play: Check in under the big lantern of Kaminarimon Gate, go shopping along Nakamise to visit the main hall, and draw lots (100 yen). Renting a kimono is a great way to take photos. If you have enough time, you can take a cruise on the Sumida River to Odaiba. Eat: Nakamise’s Ningyo yaki and fried steamed buns are classics. For sukiyaki, go to Asakusa Imahan, for tempura, go to Daikokuya, and for dessert, go to Umeen. Buy: Nakamise’s souvenirs such as thunder and senbei; the nearby Kappabashi Prop Street is a paradise for kitchenware lovers.
sensoji.desc: The oldest temple in Tokyo: First go through the Kaminarimon gate with red lanterns, and walk along the Nakamise shopping street to the main hall. Next to it is the five-story pagoda, which is suitable for strolling around in kimono.
details: Pilgrimage route (follow this order)

Kaminarimon Gate (picture the big lantern first, with a carved wooden dragon on the bottom) → Nakamise Shopping Street about 250 meters → Hozomon Gate (4.5-meter large straw sandals hanging behind the door) → "bathe" incense in the incense burner in front of the main hall → Visit the main hall (inject ¥5 coins) → Five-storied pagoda and Asakusa Shrine on the left. Asking for a lottery ticket costs ¥100 once. If you draw an evil lottery ticket, tie the paper to the lottery holder next to it to solve the evil situation. Do not take it home.
Openness and fees

All admissions are free, and the class is open from 6:00–17:00 (opens at 6:30 from October to March). Most Nakamise shops open around 10:00 and close in the evening; if you want to take aerial shots of Kaminarimon, you have to arrive before 7:00 in the morning, and tour groups flock in after 10:00.
Eating and shopping (refined)

Nakamise: Kimura family kyoto yaki, Funawa taro yoghurt, Kameya pancakes; the old shop area on Chuchujutsu Street: Kameju Dorayaki (queuing up almost every day), Mangando yam spade yaki. Kimono experience: There are a lot of rental shops around Asakusa Station, starting from about ¥3,500 including a simple hairstyle. Wearing a kimono and walking around Nakamise is a classic way to do it (reserve weekend tickets in advance).
Practical tips

On the other side of the Sumida River, you can take pictures of Asakusa and the Skytree in the same frame; there is a free observation deck on the 8th floor of the Asakusa Culture and Tourism Center, facing the panoramic view of Nakamise. The most crowded times are at noon, and the light and flow of people are the friendliest in the early morning and evening.

tower.facts: 333 meters high · Completed in 1958 · About 9 meters taller than the Eiffel Tower
tower.hist: The Comprehensive Radio Tower, built in 1958 and designed by structuralist Tataka Naito, was modeled after the Eiffel Tower in Paris but taller and lighter. It was responsible for TV wave transmission in the Kanto region until 2012, after which the main function was taken over by Skytree. The international orange and white colors of the tower are the logo colors stipulated in the aviation law.
tower.now: Play: Main Observation Deck + Top Observation Deck (additional tickets are required for the top). There is RED° Tokyo Tower (esports/amusement) and aquarium in FootTown under the tower. You can also visit Zojoji Temple on foot. Eat: The FootTown Food Court is convenient, but if you are more particular, go to the nearby Azabutai-no-oka Restaurant Floor, which will be newly opened in 2023. Buy: The official FootTown store has Tokyo Tower limited merchandise, and Azabudai Hills has a large number of brand flagship stores.
tower.desc: The 333-meter-high red iron tower, with its red and white steel frame as its symbol (the same color as the real thing), is especially beautiful when lit up at night. The bottom of the tower and the two observation decks are worth seeing.
details: Floor Guide · Tower FootTown

The 5-story building FootTown at the foot of the tower: 1F is the entrance, ticket office and coffee bar; 2F is the official store and souvenirs; 3F-5F is the immersive entertainment facility RED° TOKYO TOWN (e-sports, VR, somatosensory games, charged according to the project). There are often markets and activities in the square directly below the tower.
Observation Deck · 150m and 250m

The Main Deck is 150m and has two floors: the lower floor has a glass floor "Lookdown Window" and a coffee bar, and the upper floor has a souvenir shop and the highest-altitude shrine "Tadao Shrine". The Top Deck is at 250m, and you need to participate in the Top Deck Tour: transfer to the dedicated elevator from 150m, equipped with a guide, drinks and an observation space decorated with mirror geometry. On a clear day, you can overlook Mount Fuji.
Tickets (current price on official website)

Main Deck (150m): Adults ¥1,500/High school students ¥1,200/Elementary and middle school students ¥900/Infants (4 years old+) ¥600, 9:00–23:00 (last admission 22:30), no reservation required. Top Deck Tour (150m＋250m): Booking on the official website costs ¥3,300 for adults and ¥3,500 at the on-site window. The guided tour is based on time slots. It is recommended to purchase online in advance. There is also a Diamond Tour that includes a lounge for ¥7,000.
Practical tips

The 600-step outdoor staircase is open on weekends and holidays (you can take the stairs up and down the main observation deck). It is interesting to look at the steel skeleton of the tower while climbing; after sunset, the entire tower lights up with a classic orange light, giving it a special color on anniversaries. Recommended evening show: take in all the daytime, dusk, and night scenes at once. Take a side trip to Zenjoji Temple and Shiba Park. The "Tower + Red Temple" is a classic position.

shibuya.facts: About 3,000 people can pass on a single green light · Known as the busiest intersection in the world
shibuya.hist: Shibuya was a post town during the Edo period, and after the installation of the statue of the loyal dog Hachiko in 1934, Hachiko-mae became the most famous meeting place in Tokyo. After the war it developed into a center of youth culture and fashion, and the omnidirectional intersection has been in use for pedestrians since 1973.
shibuya.now: Play: SHIBUYA SKY Rooftop Observation Deck overlooks the intersection (be sure to book online in advance), take photos with the loyal dog Hachiko, and go shopping and rest in Miyashita Park. Eat: There are many famous ramen shops such as Ichiran and Ippudo. Shibuya Yokocho is suitable for drinking in the evening. There is a restaurant with a view on the upper floor of Scramble Square. Buy: SHIBUYA109 (young women's clothing), Shibuya PARCO (Nintendo TOKYO, Pokémon Center), Scramble Square, MEGA Don Quijote, Loft, and Tokyu Hands.
shibuya.desc: The world-famous omnidirectional intersection allows thousands of people to cross the road at the same time when the light turns green. The cylindrical SHIBUYA 109 opposite and the wall-to-wall large screen are the most common Tokyo scenes in Japanese dramas.
details: Floor Guide · SHIBUYA SKY

Located in the east building of Scramble Square: 14F ticket entrance → 45F indoor cloister SKY GALLERY → 46F rooftop SKY STAGE: 360° open-air platform with glass check-in corner, apron lawn and lying net. B2-14F in the same building are shopping malls and restaurants on 12/13F. Surroundings: PARCO 6F has Nintendo Tokyo and Pokémon Center, and under the roof of Miyashita Park is the Shibuya Yokocho Food Street.
Tickets (current price on official website)

SHIBUYA SKY is all by reservation: official website adult tickets are ¥2,700 before 15:00 and ¥3,400 after 15:00; 14F on-site window is ¥300 each; children (6-12 years old) ¥1,200 are only sold on site, and preschool is free. Tickets go on sale at 0:00 Japan time 14 days before the admission date, and are divided into 20-minute time slots. The sunset venue is often sold out in a few minutes, so set your alarm in advance.
One day route

Morning: Hachiko Statue and intersection (watch the crowds on the rooftop of MAGNET or the second floor of Starbucks) → Hang out in PARCO and Miyashita Park → Go to SKY in the evening to watch the sunset and night view with lights → Return to Shibuya Yokocho or Dogenzaka Izakaya for dinner. Bags, hats and tripods are not allowed on the roof. There are coin lockers on 46F, so prepare coins first.

shinjuku.facts: Shinjuku Station has an average of about 3 million passengers a day and is recognized by Guinness as the busiest station in the world.
shinjuku.hist: The place name comes from "Naito Shinjuku", a sleeping camp established in 1698. After the Great Kanto Earthquake, the commercial focus moved westward, and Shinjuku gradually emerged. Since the 1960s, super-high-rise buildings have been built in the West Exit area. In 1991, the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building was completed and the metropolitan government moved here. The Cocoon Tower (Mode Academy) became a new symbol of the West Exit.
shinjuku.now: Play: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observation Deck is free and open until late at night, you can see Godzilla’s head in Kabukicho, and Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden is suitable for walking and picnicking. Eat: The Yakitori Izakaya in Yokocho has the most atmosphere. There are many famous shops in the ramen battle area, and the underground food floor of the department store has rich choices. Buy: Isetan (the benchmark department store in Tokyo), LUMINE, NEWoMan. Young people like shopping. For electronics, go to Yodobashi and Bic Camera.
meta: Recommended to stay for half a day
shinjuku.desc: Tokyo's largest transportation hub. The Cocoon Tower at the west exit and the twin-tower-shaped Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building are the two most recognizable buildings here, while the east exit is a department store and izakaya street.
details: Zoning guide (find the direction first)

Bounded by the station: West Exit - Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building, cocoon-shaped Cocoon Tower, high-rise hotels, suitable for viewing buildings and climbing to the observation deck; East Exit - Kabukicho, Mode Yokocho, Golden Gai, home of nightlife; South Exit - NEWoMan and Takashimaya, the most convenient for shopping. The station is a famous maze: follow the "West Exit/Southeast Exit/New South Exit" signs on the ground, and the colors of the lines (JR green, Keio pink, Odakyu blue) are the most reliable.
Free observation deck

The 45F North and South Observation Rooms of the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building No. 1 are 202 meters high. Free admission from 9:30 to 23:00. You can see Mount Fuji on a clear day. There is also a grand piano that is often played. More cost-effective than the paid observatory, it is the best way to open up to the Shinjuku skyline.
Practical tips

The lockers in the station are often full during peak periods, so you can use ecbo cloak or hotel storage instead; the express bus to Kawaguchiko and Hakone is at Busta Shinjuku 4F at the south exit; the Limousine Airport bus stops at major hotels at the west exit. Choose the West Exit or South Exit for accommodation, as it will take the least effort to drag your luggage.

akiba.facts: Started as an electrical black market after the war. Now it is a world-renowned animation and game cultural center.
akiba.hist: After World War II, vendors selling radio parts gathered in Akihabara. In the 1950s, it developed into a home electronics street, known as the "Electric Town". Since the 1990s, computers, games and animation peripherals have gradually become the protagonists. In the 2000s, maid coffee and other businesses have emerged, transforming this place into a mecca for otaku culture.
akiba.now: Play: Visit the electronics street and handicraft stores, experience maid coffee, catch dolls at the GiGO game center, and Central Street becomes a pedestrian street on Sunday afternoons. Eat: There are many ramen shops and curry specialty shops such as Kyushu Hoshino. The omurice rice at Maid Café is a unique experience. Buy: Yodobashi Akiba is a giant electronics store. For second-hand items, go to Sofmap and Surugaya. For figures, go to Radio Kaikan and Mandarake. You can go shopping at the gashapon specialty store for a long time.
akiba.desc: The center of electronics, animation and game culture, Central Street is lined with high-rise buildings with colorful signs, video game stores and gashapon machines. It turns into a pedestrian street on Sunday afternoons.
details: Store and floor guide

Yodobashi Akiba (huge building on the east side of the station): 1–6F electrical appliances, mobile phones and computers, 7F catering, 8F toy model and gashapon area, 9F rest area. Radio Hall (next to the station): 1F gashapon peripherals, 2-3F figures, 4F Kaiyangdo, and 5F second-hand shop. It is the core building for Taobao figures. animate's main store is in the northern section of Central Street (the most popular for women); Surugaya and Mandarake are hidden in the alleys on both sides of the main street.
How to play and price reference

A gashapon costs ¥300–500 per time, so prepare enough coins; arcades (GiGO, etc.) are divided into dolls, music games and fighting areas by floor; maid coffee process: choose a set meal (drinks + meals + photos starting from about ¥2,500) → read cute slogans when ordering. Most stores prohibit selfies and can only buy in-store photos. You must bring your original passport for tax-free checkout.
Practical tips

Sunday 13:00–17:00 Central Street becomes a paradise for pedestrians. Stand in the middle of the street and take photos for the best photos. When buying electrical appliances, first confirm the voltage (Japanese 100V) and overseas warranty coverage. Large items can be delivered to the airport or hotel, so don’t carry them around while shopping.

ueno.facts: Opened in 1873 · One of the earliest parks in Japan · Home to many museums and art galleries
ueno.hist: This place was originally within Kan'eiji Temple and was designated as one of Japan's first parks in 1873. After that, Ueno Zoo (1882), Tokyo National Museum, etc. were completed one after another, gradually forming the cultural center of Tokyo; the Saigo Takamori statue at the entrance was built in 1898 and is the symbol of the park.
ueno.now: Play: You can see the Tokyo National Museum, the Museum of Western Art, and the National Science Museum all day long, you can see giant pandas at Ueno Zoo, and you can go boating at Shinobazu Pond to see Bentendo. Eat: Eat at Ame Yokochori’s seafood donburi, skewers, and fruit stalls while walking, and the old-fashioned Western cuisine Seiyōken is also next to the park. Buy: Ame Yokocho is a cheap market (cosmetics, snacks, shoes and clothing are all cheap), and Takeiya is a discount department store that locals love to shop.
meta: Recommended to stay for half a day
ueno.desc: The cultural district is home to museums, art galleries, and zoos. In front of it is the Tokyo National Museum Main Building, which is filled with cherry blossoms in spring. Take the Skyliner directly from Narita to here.
details: Building and ticket reference

National Museum: Main Building (Japanese Art) + Oriental Building + Heisei Building, permanent exhibitions are about ¥1,000 for adults, special exhibitions are purchased separately; National Museum of Western Art permanent exhibitions are about ¥500 (the building itself is a World Heritage Site of Le Corbusier); National Science Museum is about ¥630; Ueno Zoo is about ¥600 (coupons are issued during popular times at the Giant Panda Museum). Most libraries are closed on Mondays.
two routes

Cultural Half Day Line: National Museum Main Building → Oriental Building → Western Art Museum → Former Iwasaki Residence Garden. Family line: Zoo (panda + monorail in the park) → Boating at Shinobazu Pond → Eat snacks and buy cosmetics at Ame Yokocho. During the cherry blossom season (end of March to early April), the park’s main avenue is the most famous cherry blossom viewing avenue in Tokyo. It is recommended to come early in the morning on weekdays.
Practical tips

For multi-park tours, you can buy passes such as "ぐるっとパス" to get a better deal; Ame Yokocho has the best souvenirs at Futaki Confectionery; taking the Keisei Skyliner from Ueno to Narita Airport is the fastest, and Keisei Ueno Station is right next to the park exit.

palace.facts: The ruins of the original Edo Castle · Became the Imperial Palace in 1888 · The East Garden is open to the public for free
palace.hist: This was once the Edo Castle of the Tokugawa Shogunate, and became the residence of the imperial family after the Meiji Restoration. The stone bridge and iron bridge at the main gate are collectively called the Double Bridge. The Fushimi oar, moat, and stone walls are all relics of the Edo Castle period and have been preserved to this day.
palace.now: Play: Free admission to Higashi Gyoen Garden to see the Edo Castle ruins and Japanese gardens, take photos in front of Niju Bridge, take a walk on the outer lawn, and go boating in Chidorigafuchi to enjoy cherry blossoms in spring are top experiences. Eat: Walk to Marunouchi and Otemachi, where there are many restaurants, or go directly to Tokyo Station to eat at the ramen street (see Tokyo Station guide). Buy: KITTE (old post office building, cultural and creative groceries and rooftop garden), Marunouchi Building and Shin-Marunouchi Building, Daimaru Tokyo Store.
palace.desc: The residence of the Emperor. What you can recognize is the white Fushimi oars on the stone wall of the moat and the double bridge in front. The East Garden is open to the public for free and is very close to Tokyo Station.
details: Zoning Guidelines

The tour is divided into three sections: Higashi Gyoen - the old Edo Castle Main Maru, Ninomaru Gardens and the stone foundation of the castle tower (free, enter through the Otemon gate, get a ticket and return it when you go out); Gaien and Niju Bridge - a classic vantage point for taking pictures of the Imperial Palace's main entrance and moat; Chidorigafuchi - along the moat, there are about 700 meters of cherry blossom tunnels and boating in spring (about ¥800/30 minutes reference).
Openness and Attention

East Imperial Garden 9:00–16:30 (varies depending on the season), closed on Mondays and Fridays (if there are holidays); tours inside the Imperial Palace require reservations in advance on the Imperial Household Agency’s official website (free, morning/afternoon sessions). The security check is strict, do not bring large luggage, there are no shops in the park, so bring your own drinking water.
half day route

Exit from the Marunouchi Exit of Tokyo Station → Yuyuki-dori → Take pictures of Nijubashi → Higashi Gyoen Otemon → Castle Tower → Exit from Kitakibashi Gate → Return to KITTE or Marunouchi Building for lunch. The journey takes approximately 2 hours and is a moderately strenuous walk, suitable for strollers.

tokyost.facts: Opened in 1914·Designed by Tatsuno Kingo·The red brick station building is a national important cultural property
tokyost.hist: Designed by architect Tatsuno Kingo, it opened in 1914. Its exterior of red bricks and white stone waistlines is representative of Meiji Western architecture. The three-story dome was burned in an air raid during World War II. The restoration project was completed in 2012 and returned to its original appearance in 1914. The decorations in the north and south domes were also restored.
tokyost.now: Play: Take a panoramic view of the red brick station building in the square in front of the station, and look up at the reliefs on the north and south domes after entering the station. The KITTE roof garden is the best place to take photos of the station building. Eat: Tokyo Ramen Street (8 famous restaurants including Rokurise Tsukemen), Tokyo Station Ichiban Street, and Gransta’s in-station delicacies. Buy: There is a Tokyo anime character street (Pokémon, Ghibli, Lego) on Ichiban Street. For souvenirs, go to Gransta and Daimaru: Tokyo Banana and NY PERFECT CHEESE are all famous products in the queue.
tokyost.desc: The red brick station building is a century-old building: its long red brick wall, white waistline and circular dome in the middle are its symbols. It is also the core hub of the Shinkansen and Narita Express NEX.
details: Site Guide·Banban Street

Tokyo Station Ichiban Street on the basement floor: Tokyo Ramen Street (8 famous stores), Tokyo Animation Avenue (Pokémon, Ghibli and other peripherals), Dessert Land and Souvenir Street. Gransta in the station is the core area for station lunch boxes and limited-edition desserts, and ecute Keiyo Street is suitable for quick shopping before catching the train. The Marunouchi station building on the ground floor is the main attraction: the relief ceilings on the north and south domes, the station square and the axis of the pass are worth taking a look at.
Food and souvenirs

For ramen street, choose Rokurisha (thick tsukemen) or Ikaruga; for the station bento, we recommend Fukagawa rice and beef-style bento. Souvenirs: TOKYO BANANA, Sugar Butter Tree, Tokyo Milk Cheese Factory, Gransta store has the most limited editions; popular items will be sold out in the afternoon, so don’t wait until the end of your schedule to buy them.
Practical tips

The 6F rooftop garden of KITTE Marunouchi is a free seat for taking panoramic views of the station building; when transferring to the Shinkansen, look for the blue sign and reserve at least 15 minutes; large luggage can be stored at the luggage counter at the Yaesu Gate or delivered directly to the hotel.

meiji.facts: Built in 1920 to commemorate Emperor Meiji and Empress Shoken, covering an area of about 70 hectares
meiji.hist: It was established in 1920 to commemorate Emperor Meiji and Empress Shoken. About 100,000 trees were planted with donations from all over Japan and have grown into a rare forest in the city center over a century. The large torii gate at the entrance is 12 meters high and is one of the largest wooden torii gates in Japan.
meiji.now: Play: Go through the forest approach to the main shrine to worship. You can often meet the wedding procession in front of the god on weekends. The sake barrel wall is a classic photo spot. The Jingu Garden (June iris) is worth visiting. Eat: There is a Sando Café restaurant inside the shrine. Harajuku is directly outside the shrine. For food, please refer to the Harajuku guide. Shopping: Walk 5 minutes to Omotesando and Takeshita Street, shopping is done in Harajuku (see Harajuku guide).
meiji.desc: This shrine is hidden in the forest in the city center. The large torii gate at the entrance is its symbol. It is close to Harajuku but quiet and solemn, and you can often encounter Japanese wedding processions.
details: Worship route

Exit JR Harajuku Station → Minami-sando → Japan’s largest wooden torii gate → Wine Barrel Wall (French wine barrels and sake barrels are displayed in contrast, a photo spot) → Kagura Hall → Visit the main hall (we often meet the wedding procession in front of the god on weekends, so you can watch the ceremony quietly). If you have more time, visit the Meiji Jingu Garden (admission costs about ¥500, the irises fields are at their peak in June) and the Treasure Hall.
Worship etiquette

Bow lightly in front of the torii gate and walk along both sides of the shrine (the Shinto is in the center); clean your hands at the hand water house in the order of left hand → right hand → rinse mouth → rinse the handle of the spoon; after inserting the coin in the main hall, pray twice, clap your hands twice and pray once. The ema is written and hung on the ema stand next to the main hall.
Practical tips

About 70 hectares of artificial forest is made up of 100,000 donated trees from all over the country. It has the fewest people and the best air in the early morning. Suggested route: Jingu Shrine in the morning (clean) → Harajuku Omotesando in the afternoon (shopping), just the same line. The first three days of the first lunar month are the most visited shrines in Japan, so try to avoid those days.

odaiba.facts: The coastal defense fort island and Rainbow Bridge that originated in the late Edo period opened to traffic in 1993
odaiba.hist: "Odaiba" originally refers to the fort island built in Edo Bay after the arrival of the black ships in 1853. After the development of the coastal city center in the 1990s, it was built as a new seaside town. The headquarters of Fuji TV moved there in 1997, and the spherical observatory in the center became the symbol of Odaiba.
odaiba.now: Play: Watch the Unicorn Gundam hourly transformation show, Fuji TV Sphere Observation Deck, watch the Rainbow Bridge at Odaiba Seaside Park, Tokyo Joypolis and Legoland Discovery Center are suitable for parents and children. Eat: Aqua City's Ramen Kokugikan brings together ramen from all over the country, and DECKS 1-chome Shopping Street is a Showa-style snack street. Buy: DiverCity (official store of Gundam Base), Aqua City, and DECKS are all large shopping malls. You can also stop by teamLab Planets in Toyosu (reservation required).
meta: Recommended to stay for half a day
odaiba.desc: Tokyo Bay Artificial Island: The big ball in the middle of the Fuji TV building, the 1:1 Gundam statue, and the Rainbow Bridge across Tokyo Bay. The night view is especially beautiful.
details: Look at the buildings one by one

The seaside park is lined up: Fuji TV (25F Sphere Observation Room "はちたま") → Aqua City (rooftop shot of the Rainbow Bridge) → DECKS (retro Odaiba 1-chome shopping street + Joypolis indoor park) → DiverCity (1:1 Unicorn Gundam, with deformation + light show on the hour) → Statue of Liberty (cast in the same shape as the French original). A little further away is the inverted pyramid of Tokyo Big Sight.
How to play and ticket reference

Fuji TV Sphere Outlook is about ¥880; Joypolis all-day pass is about ¥5,000 (tickets are cheaper in the evening); the Rainbow Bridge Trail is free and open (about 1.7km, it is best to see the sunset and the skyline on the other side in the evening, please pay attention to the closing time); the seaside park beach can tread water but not swim. Duty-free counters are concentrated in DiverCity and Aqua City.
One day route

In the morning, watch Gundam + shopping at DiverCity → Lunch at Aqua City Ramen Kokugikan → In the afternoon, go to Joypolis or DECKS Nostalgic Shopping Street → Watch the sunset at the Rainbow Bridge in Seaside Park in the evening → Return to DiverCity in the evening to watch the Gundam night show. Please sit in the first row when taking the Yurikamome Line. The scenery on the cross-sea section is like a free roller coaster.

roppongi.facts: Roppongi Hills Opened in 2003 · Mori Tower is 238 meters high
roppongi.hist: The place name comes from the legend of six pine trees here during the Edo period. After the war, it developed into an international area due to its proximity to embassies of various countries. Roppongi Hills opened in 2003. The Mori Art Museum and high-rise observation deck have made it a landmark for art and night views. The National New Museum of Art is also within walking distance.
roppongi.now: Play: Mori Art Museum + Tokyo City View Observation Deck (you can see Tokyo Tower up close), watch exhibitions at the National New Museum of Art, and take a walk in Keyakizaka in the evening. Eat: Roppongi is a Michelin-density area. The restaurants in Roppongi Hills and Tokyo Midtown range from ramen to French food. Roppongi Yokocho is suitable for late-night snacks. Buy: Roppongi Hills (luxury brands + groceries), Tokyo Midtown (high-end brands and design stores), don’t miss the Keyakizaka illuminations during the Christmas season.
roppongi.desc: Areas with art galleries, observation decks and nightlife. The slightly slimmer Mori Building is the main building of Roppongi Hills, and the top observation deck can overlook Tokyo Tower.
details: Buildings and Premises

Roppongi Hills: Mori Building 52F Mori Art Museum + Tokyo City View (indoor), the rooftop Sky Deck is 270m open-air; downstairs there is the Mori Garden and Asahi TV. Tokyo Midtown: 21_21 DESIGN SIGHT, Suntory Museum of Art and the entire lawn. The National Museum of Art is a wavy glass curtain wall designed by Kisho Kurokawa. The permanent area is free and special exhibitions are charged. The three places form the "Roppongi Art Triangle" and can be connected on foot.
Ticket reference

The special exhibition at the Mori Art Museum is about ¥2,000 for adults (it varies depending on the exhibition), the city view is about ¥2,000, and the Sky Deck is about ¥500 extra. There are often two-museum packages; the special exhibition at the National New Museum of Art is about ¥1,500. Many art museums are closed on Tuesdays (except during exhibition periods), so check the official website before traveling.
Night tour route

In the evening, relax on the Midtown Lawn → Watch the Tokyo Tower lights up at Nookaoka Observation Deck → Dinner at the Mori Garden → Walk around Keyakizaka (the entire street is a blue light tunnel during the winter lighting season). The bars are concentrated in the alleys to the west of the station. Before entering, check to see if there is a seating fee.

ikebukuro.facts: Sunshine City Complex Completed 1978–1980 · Sunshine 60 Height 227 meters
ikebukuro.hist: Ikebukuro developed with the opening of the railway during the Meiji period, and after the war it became a deputy city center on the west side of the Yamanote Line. Sunshine City, built since 1978, includes an aquarium, planetarium and observatory. When its main building, Sunshine 60, was built, it was one of the tallest skyscrapers in Asia. In recent years, the east exit's anime-related shops (Otome Street) are also famous.
ikebukuro.now: Play: Sunshine Aquarium and Planetarium, Tenbou Park Observation Deck, Otome Street is a female-oriented anime mecca, and animate Ikebukuro main store is the world's largest anime peripheral store. Eat: There are always queues for Wudi Ramen, but it is worth it. There are many choices in the underground food floors of Sunshine City and Tobu and Seibu Department Stores. Buy: Sunshine City alpa/ALTA, animate, Surugaya Otomekan, Don Quijote and Bic Camera at the west exit.
ikebukuro.desc: A cost-effective accommodation and shopping area, the Sunshine City tower at the east entrance is a landmark, with an aquarium and an observation deck inside.
details: Sunshine City Guide

Sunshine City Complex: Sunshine 60 Building + Specialty Store Alpa + Aquarium + Observation Deck. The Sunshine Aquarium is on the roof, and its sign is "Penguins in the Sky" (a penguin tank swimming overhead). Tickets are about ¥2,600 for reference. Reservations are required during peak seasons; the Sunshine 60 Observation Deck has been transformed into the free-entry Tenbou Park rooftop park (with coffee and lawn). In the same area are the Sunshine Prince Hotel and the Ancient Oriental Museum.
animate and otome road

animate Ikebukuro main store is the world's largest animation store: 1F new issues and event areas, 2-3F comics and CDs, upper-level drawing materials and doujinshi, with the most comprehensive collection for women. Going east from the store is Otome Street: Surugaya Otome Hall, K-BOOKS and themed coffees are clustered together; male-oriented shops are concentrated in the East Exit Street area. If you go shopping together, Ikebukuro will be the anime version of Akihabara.
Practical tips

The east and west exits of Ikebukuro Station are separated by the station passage. Look for the "East Exit (North)/West Exit (Central)" signs to identify the opposite directions; the airport bus runs from the West Exit Hotel Area to Haneda and Narita; this is the most cost-effective area for accommodation in the Yamanote Line's Western Ring.

shinagawa.facts: Opened in 1872 · One of the earliest railway stations in Japan
shinagawa.hist: When Japan's first railway (Shimbashi-Yokohama) opened in 1872, Shinagawa Station was one of the original stations. Further back, in the Edo period, this was the first accommodation on the Tokaido, "Shinagawa-juku", with many brigades and teahouses.
shinagawa.now: Play: Maxell Aqua Park Shinagawa Aquarium (dolphin show + light and shadow show), Shinagawa Shrine and Tokaido Shinagawa Street are suitable for walking. Eat: "Pinda Ramen" on the site gathers 7 famous ramen restaurants, and ecute Shinagawa also has great souvenirs and bento boxes. Purchase: The main businesses in the station are: ecute, Wing Takanawa, Atre Shinagawa. It is most suitable to shop before and after changing trains.
shinagawa.desc: The Keikyu Line is the first station entering the city from Haneda. In front of the station are rows of glass high-rise hotels. It is very convenient to transfer to the Yamanote Line and Shinkansen.
details: Station features

Shinagawa is a "transportation hub + station life" type station: the commercial ecute in the station is extremely dense with Shinagawa souvenirs and lunch boxes, and you can buy them all 10 minutes before catching the Shinkansen; the ramen area "Pinda" has 7 stores; the Takanawa exit is a hotel group and an aquarium, and the Konan exit is an office building and canal office area. The division of labor is clear: the Tokaido Shinkansen goes to Nagoya and Osaka, and the Keikyu Line goes to Haneda in about 15 minutes.
Peripheral gameplay

Maxell Aqua Park Shinagawa (in Shinagawa Prince Hotel): The dolphin show that combines sound and light is the signature. Tickets are about ¥2,500. Please refer to the announcement on the day for the show. A 10-minute walk to the south is the old Tokaido "Shinagawa-juku" old street and Shinagawa Shrine, which retains the atmosphere of an Edo post station; Tennosu Island by the canal has cafes and galleries converted from warehouses, which is suitable for transfer breaks.
Transfer tips

It's fastest to transfer to the Yamanote Line and take the central ticket gate; go to Haneda to catch an early flight, the first Keikyu train leaves around 5:00 (confirm before departure); the south exit side of the lockers in the station is usually empty. Shinagawa Station does not have the shopping attributes of Akihabara. It is positioned as a transportation-oriented accommodation area with efficient transfer + one-night stay.

ginza.facts: The place name comes from the silver coin foundry in the Edo period. The Wako Bell Tower was built in 1932.
ginza.hist: In the Edo period, there was a "Ginza Yakusho" where silver coins were minted here, hence the place's name. After a fire in 1872, Ginza was rebuilt in a Western style into a street of brick Western-style buildings, which became a symbol of civilization. Since then, it has gradually formed a business structure in which high-end department stores and century-old shops coexist.
ginza.now: Play: Central Street becomes a pedestrian street on weekend afternoons. Check in in front of the Wako Clock Tower. You can buy a single-act ticket to watch a show at Kabukiza. You can rest and enjoy the scenery at the GINZA SIX rooftop garden. Eat: High-end sushi and Western food are densely packed with old stores. Shiseido Parlour’s omurice and Kimura’s red bean bread are century-old classics. The underground food floor of the department store is also exciting. Buy: Ginza Mitsukoshi, Matsuya, GINZA SIX (including Tsutaya Bookstore), Itoya Stationery Main Store, MUJI Global Flagship Store, UNIQLO Global Flagship Store (entire 12th floor).
ginza.desc: Tokyo's most upscale shopping district. The Wako Department Store clock tower at the 4-chome intersection is a symbol of Ginza, and Chuo Street turns into a pedestrian street on weekends.
details: Alignment of intersection landmarks

The Ginza 4-chome intersection is the heart of Ginza: Wako Department Store (clock tower, look at the clock face on the hour) and Mitsukoshi across the road, and opposite is GINZA SIX. The Tsutaya Bookstore and rooftop garden on the top floor of GINZA SIX are open for free, overlooking the Ginza street view. To the south is the 5-chome UNIQLO global flagship store (12th floor), and to the north is the stationery and long-established shop area.
Shopping refinement

Stationery: The entire 12 floors of the Itoya main store are stratified by category, with pens and wallets on the upper floors; department stores: Matsuya looks at Japanese design selections, and the Mitsukoshi B1 food floor is the main battlefield for souvenirs; affordable: Don Quijote Ginza main store is open until late at night. Department store duty-free processing is available at designated counters. Please queue up during popular periods and reserve time.
Food and Tips

Long-established line: Kimura's red bean bread (there is a cafe on the 2F of the main store), Shiseido Parlor omurice; affordable line: B1/B2 food floor of each department store. Weekends 12:00–17:00 Central Tongbian Pedestrian Paradise. Standing in the middle of the street is the most stable place to take photos. To watch Kabuki, please book your tickets in advance on the Kabukiza official website, as there are only a limited number of theater seats available on that day.

harajuku.facts: Takeshita-dori is about 350 meters long and has been the birthplace of youth culture since the 1970s.
harajuku.hist: Around the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, Harajuku began to gather fashionable people. In the 1970s, Takeshita Street became a shopping street for teenagers. "Harajuku style" fashion, vintage clothing and crepe culture spread from here to the whole country. Omotesando next to it is famous for its zelkova-lined streets and famous buildings. The two streets are one vulgar and the other elegant.
harajuku.now: Play: Takeshita Street is a place where you can browse small shops, take photos of photos, and eat crepes. The Omotesando area is an architectural tour (flagship stores of major brands are themselves attractions), and Meiji Jingu Shrine is in constant motion. Eat: Marion crepe is made by Takeshita Tōgenzu, Harajuku Gyoza House is affordable and delicious, and there are many cafes in the alleys of Omotesando. Buy: Laforet Harajuku, Tokyu Plaza Omotesando Harajuku, Omotesando Hills (luxury brands), Kiddy Land toys and affordable fashion brands WEGO are also in this line.
harajuku.desc: Takeshita Street is full of young and trendy shops and crepe stalls. The colorful arches at the entrance are crowded with people on weekends, and the Meiji Shrine next to it is constantly moving and quiet.
details: How to divide the three streets?

Takeshita Street: About 150 meters of trendy streets (crepes, vintage clothes, idol items), the least crowded before 11 a.m.; Meiji Jingu Shrine is on the west side of Harajuku Station, visit first and then go shopping; Omotesando: Both sides of the boulevard are lined with brand flagships and architectural works. The three lines are in the shape of a "herringbone", and it takes half a day to complete one circle.
Omotesando Architecture Tour

Omotesando Hills (Tadao Ando, spiral ramp), the mirrored entrance of Tokyu Plaza Harajuku, GYRE (Kengo Kuma), the crystal glass tower of Prada Aoyama store, Nezu Museum (Kengo Kuma Bamboo Forest Entrance + Garden Café). Architecture fans will not be disappointed if they follow this line and slowly look at each building.
Shopping and food

Laforet Harajuku is a trendsetter for youth brands (styles are divided by floors); Kiddy Land has four floors of toys and character peripherals; for crepes, the queue is shorter at the old store in the middle of Takeshita Street; if you want to sit down and have waffle brunch at Bills in the alley of Omotesando, or walk 8 minutes to Minami Aoyama Blue Bottle Coffee.

toyosu.facts: Opened in 2018·Replaced Tsukiji Market·With a large green square on the roof
toyosu.hist: To solve the problem of aging facilities at Tsukiji Market, the Tokyo Metropolitan Government moved the wholesale market to the Toyosu artificial island in October 2018. The market consists of three buildings: fishery wholesale, fishery unloading, and green fruit. Tsukiji's off-site market remains in its original location, forming a new pattern of "Toyosu inside + Tsukiji outside".
toyosu.now: Play: Go to the market passage in the early morning to watch the tuna auction (you need to be selected in advance for close-up visits), watch the bay view at Toyosu Park, and be within walking distance of teamLab Planets (be sure to make a reservation in advance). Eat: Enjoy sushi breakfast at old restaurants such as Yamato Sushi in the market. The newly opened "Thousands of Customers" in 2024 is an Edo-style food street, and there is also a foot bath where you can soak your feet and watch the sea. Buy: A popular souvenir shop, and a little further away is the LaLaport Toyosu shopping mall.
meta: It is recommended to stay for 2 hours (note the market closing days)
toyosu.desc: Tokyo Kitchen: The white building is characterized by an entire rooftop lawn. You can watch the tuna auction and have sushi breakfast in the early morning, and pay attention to the closed days.
details: Market play

Watch the tuna auction: There is a free viewing channel on the 3F of the Aquatic Products Wholesale Building. You can overlook the auction house through the glass. It is busiest around 5:30 in the morning. The viewing platform on the lower floor is a lottery system, and you need to register in advance on the official website. On-site dining is on 3-4F: Sushi Dai and Yamato Sushi start queuing up at 6 o'clock; if you don't want to queue up, go to the seafood rice bowl and snack street that is crowded with customers outside the venue, so it's easier to open until evening.
Thousands of customers come to teamLab

Thousands of customers come here (opening in 2024): Edo-style shopping street + free footbath on the top floor (soak your feet while looking at Tokyo Bay, bring your own or buy a towel). teamLab Planets is in Shin-Toyosu, about a 10-minute walk away (all reservations required, about ¥3,800 for adults): In the wading exhibition area, please roll up your trousers and don’t wear long skirts. LaLaport Toyosu is on the other side of the station, with a sea view restaurant and complete facilities for children.
One day route

Watch the auction + sushi breakfast in the early morning → Thousands of customers come to footbath snacks → teamLab (book the morning session in advance) → LaLaport lunch → Take the Yurikamome Line to Odaiba to watch the sunset. Pay attention to market closing days: mostly Wednesdays and Sundays, the market and most shops are closed, so be sure to check the official website calendar before traveling.

disney.facts: Opened in 1983, the first Disneyland outside the United States
disney.hist: Tokyo Disneyland opened in Urayasu City, Chiba Prefecture in April 1983. It was Disney's first park outside the United States. The ocean-themed Tokyo DisneySea opened in 2001. The two parks and the hotel complex form the Tokyo Disney Resort; the approximately 51-meter-tall Cinderella Castle is the central symbol of the park.
disney.now: Play: The park has priority in the new areas "Beauty and the Beast", Splash Mountain, and Thunder Mountain; the ocean has priority in Soaring: Fantasy Voyage, Terror Tower, and Center of the Earth Adventure. Get express passes on the official app before entering the park. Eat: Popcorn has a variety of limited flavors and is suitable for buying on the go. You need to make a reservation in advance for the Duffy-themed restaurant in the ocean. Purchase: You can buy limited-edition merchandise (the most complete of the Duffy family) at World Market and Ocean Shops in the park. You can buy official merchandise without tickets at Ikspiari Shopping Town outside the park and at Bon Voyage in front of Maihama Station.
meta: Recommended to stay for a full day
disney.desc: Disney Resort located in Urayasu, Chiba. The Cinderella Castle at the entrance has pink walls and blue spires. It takes about 15 minutes to get to Maihama from Tokyo Station on the Keiyo Line.
details: Tickets (current price on official website)

One-day passport is priced from ¥8,900–12,400 for adults, from ¥7,400 for teenagers (12–17 years old), from ¥5,300 for children (4–11 years old), and free for children under 3 years old. Tickets are not sold onsite at the park and can only be purchased in advance on the official website or official app (on sale at 14:00 on the same day 2 months before the park entry date). The price difference between weekdays and Saturdays is up to ¥3,500/person, so choose a date based on your budget.
Game system

Open the official app before entering the park: free "priority admission tickets" can reserve time slots for popular projects; paid DPA fast passes are about ¥1,500-2,500/item (Beauty and the Beast, Splash Mountain, Ocean's Dream Spring Township projects, etc.). Those who only come here once are worth buying 1-2. For the admission rules of Fantasy Spring Township, please refer to the app announcement on the day, and confirm before entering the park. The parade and evening show will take place in the square in front of the castle 40 minutes in advance.
One-day route · branch version

The park: Go straight to Beauty and the Beast when the park opens → Thunder Mountain → Splash Mountain → Go back to World Market for lunch and shopping → In the afternoon, it’s a small world, The Haunted Mansion, Pirates of the Caribbean + daytime cruise → The castle light show ends at night. Ocean: First visit to Fantasy Springs (Frozen, Rapunzel) → Adventure to the Center of the Earth → Indiana Jones → Mediterranean Harbor Water Show in the evening → Take the tram and railway back to the American seaside. For the return trip, it will be least crowded if you leave the park 30 minutes before the last bus.

hnd.facts: Opened in 1931 · Approximately 15 kilometers from the city center · Ranked first in domestic passenger volume in Japan
hnd.hist: Opened as Tokyo's first civilian airport in 1931, it was taken over by the US military after the war and returned to Japan in 1952. After the opening of Narita Port in 1978, Haneda mainly handled domestic routes; after the opening of the new international terminal (now Terminal 3) in 2010, the international routes were greatly expanded, and Haneda once again became Tokyo's air gateway.
hnd.now: Fun: The "Edo Koji" in Terminal 3 is a replica of the streets of Edo, which is suitable for taking pictures. The observation decks of each terminal can watch planes take off and land up close. If you have a long layover, you can go to the Haneda Airport Garden to soak in the "Izumi Sky Bath" hot spring. Eat: Edo Alley is concentrated on Japanese food, and there are many restaurants and gourmet souvenirs in Haneda Airport Garden (opening in 2023). Purchase: Apart from duty-free shops, the souvenirs on Edo Alley and Airport Garden are the most Japanese. You can buy them all at one stop before catching your flight.
meta: It is recommended to arrive 2–3 hours in advance for international flights
hnd.desc: Located in Narita City, Chiba Prefecture, about 60 kilometers from the city center (map has been compressed). To get into the city, Skyliner, Narita Express NEX or Access Express are the first choices.
details: Terminal Guide

There is a free shuttle bus between T1 (JAL domestic line) and T2 (ANA domestic line), and there are rooftop observation decks to watch planes taking off and landing. T3 International Line: 4F "Edo Koji" is an Edo-style commercial street, where you can also eat sushi ramen on late-night flights; 5F observation deck and animation surrounding area. The Haneda Airport Garden next to T3 has a rooftop hot spring "Izumi Tenku no Yu" and a hotel complex. You can take a bath and rest before and after a red-eye flight (hot spring charges apply).
Comparison of transportation into the city

The Keikyu Line takes about 15 minutes to Shinagawa and costs around ¥300, and is the fastest to get into the city; the monorail to Hamamatsucho takes about 18 minutes and costs around ¥500; the Limousine bus to Tokyo Station and Shinjuku takes about 45–75 minutes and costs around ¥3,200 (it’s easiest to take your luggage directly to the hotel); a taxi to the city center is about ¥7,000–9,000 (surcharge late at night). If you live in the Tokyo Station and Shinagawa areas, choose Keikyu. If you live in Shinjuku or Ikebukuro, consider taking the bus.
Practical tips

International late-night arrival: T3 has a 24-hour convenience store and rest area; allow more than 90 minutes for international to domestic transfers; the duty-free shops after departure in T3 have the most comprehensive selection of limited souvenirs, so don’t just buy them before departure.

nrt.facts: Opened in 1978 · Approximately 60 kilometers from the city center · Tokyo’s main international gateway
nrt.hist: In order to share the pressure of Haneda's international line, the port was opened in Narita City, Chiba Prefecture in 1978. Its construction process triggered a long-term local residents' movement and is an important page in Japan's aviation history. Since then, it has been gradually expanded to three terminals and has been responsible for most of Tokyo's international routes for a long time.
nrt.now: Fun: Watch the planes at the observation deck of Terminal 1. If you have enough waiting time (more than 4 hours), you can take a 10-minute drive to Naritasan Shinshoji Temple to visit the old streets. Eat: The restaurant streets in Terminals 1 and 2 offer sushi, ramen, and eel rice. The Kawafyo eel rice on the Shinshoji Temple is a century-old famous restaurant. Buy: Buy cosmetics and electrical appliances at Fa-So-La duty-free shop. Narita Airport’s exclusive souvenir and animation peripheral shops are also worth visiting.
meta: It is recommended to arrive 3 hours in advance for international flights
nrt.desc: Disney Resort located in Urayasu, Chiba. The Cinderella Castle at the entrance has pink walls and blue spires. It takes about 15 minutes to get to Maihama from Tokyo Station on the Keiyo Line.
details: Terminal Guide

T1 (mainly Star Alliance): 5F observatory, Pokémon store and animation area, the station is in B1; T2 (ANA, etc.): 4F commercial floor is densely packed with shops, and B1 has a capsule hotel for nine hours; T3 is an LCC dedicated terminal with simple facilities. It takes about 10 minutes to walk to T2. The observation deck at T1 is a good place to watch planes take off and land, and you can go shopping if you have a long layover.
Comparison of transportation into the city

The fastest Keisei Skyliner to Nippori and Ueno is 41 minutes, about ¥2,570 (all reserved seats); the Access Express to Asakusa and Shinagawa is about ¥1,270 and up; the Narita Express N'EX to Tokyo Station is about 53 minutes and about ¥3,070 (foreign tourists preferentially choose when round-trip discount tickets are more cost-effective); the highway bus to Tokyo Station is about ¥1,300 and up, 75–100 Minutes and most luggage friendly. Choosing a route based on accommodation location is more important than just time.
Practical tips

Transfer or long waiting time: a half-day trip to Naritasan Shinshoji Temple (get off at Keisei-Narita Station, the old street is famous for eel rice, and it takes 10 minutes by train from the airport); large luggage can be sent to the hotel via airport express delivery (next day delivery); please arrive 3 hours in advance for your return flight, as the morning is the peak time for T1/T2 security check.

toudai.facts: Founded in 1877 · Japan’s first national university · Hongo Campus: Akamon, Yasuda Lecture Hall, Ginkgo Avenue
toudai.hist: Its predecessor was the merger of Tokyo Kaisei School and Tokyo Medical School in 1877, making it the first modern university in Japan. Akamon was built in 1827 as the guardian gate of the Kaga Domain to marry the shogun's daughter. It is now a national important cultural property and a symbol of Todai. Yasuda Lecture Hall was donated by industrialist Zenjiro Yasuda and completed in 1925. Its Gothic clock tower dominates the skyline of the Hongo campus. Natsume Soseki's novel "Sanshiro" gave the school's heart character pond the name "Sanshiro Pond".
toudai.now: [Play] Enter the school from Akamon, walk along Ginkgo Avenue to Yasuda Lecture Hall, and then go around Sanshiro Pond and the General Library; the ginkgo is most beautiful in late November when it turns yellow. [Eat] The central cafeteria on campus is open to the public, and you can get student meals for a few hundred yen; there are also long-established soba noodles and cafes in Hongo-sanchome. [Buy] Dongda Students’ Association (cooperative) has Dongda-limited stationery, chocolates and ‘Akamon’ themed peripherals, which are difficult to buy outside the campus.
toudai.desc: Japan's first national university, the Hongo Campus' Akamon, Yasuda Lecture Hall and Ginkgo Avenue are the most bookish scenery in Tokyo. The campus can be visited freely.
details: Campus tour route

You can freely visit the entire campus (the interior of the teaching building is generally not open): Akamon (south side) → Ginkgo Avenue → Yasuda Lecture Hall → Comprehensive Library → Sanshiro Pond → Exit from the main gate or Longgang Gate, the whole journey takes about 1 hour. The interior of Yasuda Lecture Hall is only open during entrance ceremonies, graduation ceremonies and public events. You can usually look at the building and clock tower.
Architectural highlights

Yasuda Lecture Hall (1925): A Gothic Revival building designed by Shozo Uchida, the central clock tower is a symbol of the town, and Yasuda Zenjiro's donation was initially anonymous. Akamon (1827): The vermilion lacquered main entrance to the daimyo's residence in the Edo period, one of the only remaining shuden gates in Tokyo. The fountain square and Gothic arches in front of the comprehensive library are the most photogenic corners of the school; don’t miss the ginkgo trees in front of the lecture hall in autumn.
Practical tips

Transportation: Take the Marunouchi Line/Oedo Line 'Hongo-sanchome' station, or the North-Nan Line 'Higashidai-mae' station, just exit the station. Side trip: It takes about 15 minutes to walk to Ueno Park, and Nezu Shrine is also within the walking circle. You can arrange a half-day cultural tour of "Ueno Museum + Tokyo University Campus". Please keep quiet in the school and do not enter the teaching area to take pictures.

waseda.facts: Founded by Okuma Shigenobu in 1882 · Okuma Lecture Hall and 125-foot Bell Tower · One of Japan’s two private buildings
waseda.hist: It was founded as Tokyo Vocational College in 1882 by Okuma Shigenobu, the founder of the Meiji period. In 1902, it was renamed Waseda University. Together with Keio, it is known as one of Japan's top private schools. Okuma Lecture Hall is a Tudor Gothic auditorium built in 1927 to commemorate the 45th anniversary of its founding. The clock tower is 125 feet (approximately 38 meters) high - derived from Okuma's '125 years of life' longevity theory. The Tsubouchi Xiaoyao Memorial Acting Museum (1928) is a rare theater-specific museum in Asia, and the Murakami Haruki Library will open in 2021 with a collection of books donated by alumnus Haruki Murakami and designed by Kengo Kuma.
waseda.now: [Play] Okuma Lecture Hall and Bronze Statue → Okuma Garden (remains of the Edo Daimyo Garden) → Theater Museum (free) → Murakami Haruki Library (free, with coffee and reading space). [Eat] Just outside the school gate is the student street: a fierce battle area for ramen, fried noodles, affordable set meals, and student cafeterias on both sides of Okuma Avenue. [Buy] The on-campus student association has limited-edition merchandise for early-school students; the ‘Waseda Festival’ in early November is the largest school festival in Japan, and the whole street is lined with stalls.
waseda.desc: The prestigious private school founded by Okuma Shigenobu, the bell tower of Okuma Lecture Hall, the Drama Museum and Murakami Haruki Library are all on the Waseda campus, and outside the school gate is a lively student street.
details: Campus tour route

Free campus tour: Main entrance → Okuma Shigenobu Bronze Statue → Okuma Lecture Hall → Okuma Garden → Drama Museum → Murakami Haruki Library, about 1 hour. The interior of the Okuma Lecture Hall is only open on event days; admission to the Theater Museum and Haruki Murakami Library is free (the Haruki Murakami Library is occasionally closed, so check the official website before traveling).
Architectural highlights

Okuma Lecture Hall (1927): Tudor Gothic auditorium. The 125-foot bell tower corresponds to Okuma Shigenobu's "125 Years of Life Theory". The Kazami Rooster on the top of the tower is a symbol in the hearts of early students. The Theater Museum is modeled after the Fortune Theater in London in the 16th century. Its white walls and black wood appearance are unique among Japanese universities. Okuma Garden retains the pond and rockery of the daimyo's mansion garden in the Edo period, and is an oasis in a high-rise area.
Practical tips

Transportation: Walk for 5 minutes from ‘Waseda’ Station on the Tozai Line, or take the nostalgic Toden Arakawa Line to ‘Waseda’ Station (the old train itself is worth experiencing). On the way: Takadanobaba is about a 15-minute walk (ramen and Tezuka Osamu murals), and Kagurazaka Old Street is also within a walk and bus ride. The Waseda Festival (early November) is extremely popular and the area around campus is very crowded on those two days.

fuji.facts: 3,776 meters above sea level · Japan’s highest peak · Listed as a World Cultural Heritage in 2013 · Last erupted in 1707
fuji.hist: Mount Fuji is a stratovolcano formed by repeated eruptions. The current cone was formed about 10,000 years ago. The last eruption was the Hoei eruption in 1707. The ancients regarded climbing Mount Fuji as a spiritual practice. During the Edo period, followers of "Fujido" spread throughout Kanto, and the Sengen Shrine at the foot of the mountain was the center of belief. It is also an eternal motif of Japanese art - Katsushika Hokusai's "Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji" and Utagawa Hiroshige's Ukiyo-e paintings make it world-famous. In 2013, it was listed as a World Cultural Heritage as an ‘object of faith and a source of art’.
fuji.now: 【Play】Mountain viewing: Lake Kawaguchi (Oishi Park, Lakeside Fuji Fuji), Arakurayama Sengen Park Five-Storied Pagoda, Oshino Hakkai, one day is enough; Mountain climbing: the most classic way to go to Yoshidaguchi during the first mountain period (early July to early September), most people sleep one night in the 78th station mountain hut to watch the sunrise. [Eat] Yamanashi local noodle ‘Hofu (ほうとう)’ is pumpkin and vegetable miso noodles. The old shops in front of Kawaguchiko Station are the most famous; there are also desserts and puddings shaped like Mount Fuji. [Buy] Kawaguchiko Station and 5th station stores: Mount Fuji-limited cookies, yokan, sake, and hiking commemorative wooden staff imprints (a ritual exclusive for climbers).
meta: It is recommended to spend a whole day to see the mountain · 2 days for climbing
fuji.desc: Japan's highest peak (3,776 meters), located approximately 100 kilometers southwest of Tokyo, location indicated on the map. At the foot of the mountain are Lake Kawaguchi and Mount Arakura Five-Storied Pagoda - the most classic angles to see Mount Fuji are in this area.
details: How to get there from Tokyo

Viewing the mountains (in the direction of Lake Kawaguchi): Take the express bus from Shinjuku Station directly to Lake Kawaguchi Station for about 2 hours (about ¥2,200 reference, reservation required); the railway is from JR Chuo Line to Otsuki and transfer to the Fujikyu Line. The limited express "Fuji Express" can go directly from Shinjuku to Lake Kawaguchi (about 2 hours). Mountaineering: During the first mountaineering period, there are buses from Shinjuku/Lake Kawaguchi directly to the Yoshidaguchi 5th station (elevation 2,300 meters). Self-driving is the most flexible, but the parking lot at the fifth station is subject to restrictions during the climbing season.
Mountaineering Guide (Yoshidaguchi)

The mountain opening period is generally from early July to early September. In other seasons, mountain huts are closed and climbing is strictly prohibited. It takes about 5-7 hours to get to the top of the mountain from the fifth station of Yoshidaguchi and about 3-4 hours to go down the mountain. The current regulations for entering the mountain on the Yamanashi side: you need to make a reservation in advance on the official website and pay the entrance fee (approximately ¥4,000, subject to the official website of the year). There are gate controls from the afternoon to the early morning. "Forced climbing to the summit overnight" projectile mountaineering has been expressly prohibited and is very dangerous. Mountain huts must be reserved in advance. The temperature difference at the top of the mountain can reach 20°C, so cold protection and headlamps are a must.
Mountain Viewing Locations and Tips

Visibility rules: winter > other seasons, early morning > afternoon, the morning when it clears up after rain is best; you can check the "Mount Fuji Visibility Forecast" website before departure. Classic camera locations: Lake Kawaguchi Oishi Park (foreground during flower season), Arakurayama Sengen Park Five-story Pagoda (398 steps up, most crowded during cherry blossom and red leaf season), Lake Kawaguchi’s ‘Reverse Fuji’ reflection when there is no wind in the early morning, Lake Motosu (the location for the thousand-yen bill pattern). In Tokyo, you can see it from the Tokyo Skytree and Tokyo Metropolitan Government Observation Deck when the weather is good.

kamakura.facts: Next to Enoshima Electric Railway's "Kamakura Kogaku-mae Station" · In front of Kamakura Prefectural University Gate No. 1 · The location where the opening theme song of "Slam Dunk" was filmed · Facing Nanarihama and Enoshima
kamakura.hist: The Enoshima Electric Railway was opened to traffic in 1902 and was a small coastal railway running between Fujisawa and Kamakura; Kamakura Kogakumae Station was opened in 1931 (first name Hisaka Station). The intersection under the ramp in front of the station is opposite the gate of Kanagawa Prefectural Kamakura High School. In 1993, the scene of Sakuragi Hanamichi waiting for the train in front of the intersection and Haruko running from the opposite side in the opening theme of the animation "Slam Dunk" made this place famous overnight. The composition of the ramp, the green and white train and the sea has remained almost unchanged for more than 30 years. Now it is the first stop on the holy land tour in the hearts of animation fans around the world.
kamakura.now: [Play] Waiting at the crossing for the green and white Enoden train to pass by slowly (every 12 minutes) is a reenactment of the famous scene in the opening film; the seaside platform of the station itself is also a good place to see Enoshima; walk eastward along the coast to Shichirigahama and Inamurazaki, and you can even see Mount Fuji on a clear day. [Eat] Highly recommend Hase's earthen pot rice specialty restaurant "Kamakura Earthen Pot Kaedena.": Take Enoden 3 stops from the trailhead to Hase Station and walk for 3 minutes, right next to the Great Buddha Shrine. The Koshihikari rice produced in Tanba Sasayama is cooked pot by pot with kelp broth. The signature salmon roe clay pot rice and crab meat and avocado clay pot rice are all excellent. The set menu comes with 7 side dishes and miso soup. Lunch starts from about ¥2,800 and reservations are not available. There will be a long line when the door opens at 11 o'clock, while supplies last - please hurry up if you want to eat. The Shichirihama area is a sea-view restaurant area, and Bills is also famous for its waffles and the old-fashioned coral reef curry. [Buy] Kamakura Station Komachi Street is home to souvenirs such as Kamakura eagles and pigeon butter cakes, and Enoden peripheral products are on sale at Kamakura Station.
meta: It is recommended to clock in 0.5–1 hour · A full day tour of Kamakura/Enoshima
kamakura.desc: The railway crossing facing the sea at the beginning of "Slam Dunk" - in front of Kamakura Prefectural High School and next to the Enoshima Electric Railway Kamakura High School Front Station. Located approximately 55 kilometers southwest of Tokyo, the location is indicated on the map.
details: Check-in crossing: camera location and etiquette

The classic camera position is on the upper section of the ramp: stand on the inside of the sidewalk and use 2x zoom to bring the crossing, tram and sea into the same frame. The train runs about every 12 minutes, and when the alarm sounds, it retreats outside the railing and waits for the train to pass. Traffic wardens are on site year-round - do not stand in the middle of a driveway or on the tracks to take photos, and do not block ramps for residents to enter and exit. In the morning, there is good light and the water is the bluest; in the evening, the backlight is suitable for shooting silhouettes and sunsets. If you want to avoid the crowds, choose before 9 a.m. on weekdays.
Highly recommended food: Kaedena, a specialty earthen pot rice restaurant.

This is the most worth a special trip to eat at this restaurant. The owner is from Washoku Itamae and is located on the second floor of Hase Station, a 3-minute walk from Hase Station (3-8-13 Kamakura Nagaya). It is just 3 stops away from Kamakura Kogakumae by taking the Enoden Express, right next to the approach to the Great Buddha and Hase-dera Temple. The rice is Koshihikari rice delivered directly from contracted farmers in Tanba Sasayama, Hyogo Prefecture. It is put into the pot after receiving the order, and is cooked pot by pot with kelp stock over an open fire. The grains are distinct and full of umami flavor. The signature dish is the earthen pot rice with grilled salmon and pickled salmon roe. The crab meat, avocado, white fish (しらす) and seasonal items are also very popular. The set meal includes 7 side dishes and miso soup, and lunch starts from ¥2,800 (reference price). Note: Reservations are not available for lunch, and there are only 24 seats. There are people queuing up before the door opens at 11:00 (order first when queuing up). The restaurant is sold out while supplies last, so be sure to get there early if you want to eat. Dinner is a claypot rice set that is completely reservation-free (tel: 0467-25-3770). It is closed irregularly, mostly on Mondays. It’s firmly ranked among the more than 1,500 restaurants in Kamakura on TripAdvisor (4.6 points), and it’s a restaurant that even locals line up for.
How to get there from Tokyo · Tickets (prices are for reference only)

The smoothest way to go: Take the JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo or Shinagawa to Kamakura (about 55–60 minutes), then change to the Enoshima Electric Railway to Kamakura Kozenmae for about 15 minutes. The one-way total is about ¥1,200 (IC reference price). Starting from Shinjuku, you can buy the Odakyu "Enoshima Kamakura Free Pass" (from Shinjuku for ¥1,640, including Odakyu round trip + unlimited rides on all Enoden lines). If you only travel along the Enoden Line, the 1-day pass "のりおりくん" is the most cost-effective for ¥800 (children ¥400). You can get on and off at Hase, Enoshima, and Inamurazaki as you like.
Side trip: Enoshima + Kamakura

Take two stops to the west to Enoshima Station, walk across the Benten Bridge to reach the island: Eshima Shrine, Iwaya Cave and Sea Candle Observation Lighthouse, half a day is just right. On the return trip, get off at Hase Station to see the Kamakura Big Buddha and Hase Temple, and finally return to Kamakura Station to visit Komachi Street to finish the day. On a clear morning in winter, you can see Mount Fuji floating on the sea from Shichirigahama to Inamurazaki. It is the most classic "sea and Fuji" in Kanto.

yokohama.facts: 296 m tall · Opened 1993 · Ferris wheel Ø 100 m · Red Brick Warehouse built 1911
yokohama.hist: This was once a Mitsubishi shipyard and a national-railway freight yard; from the 1980s it was reclaimed and rebuilt as the 'Minato Mirai 21' waterfront district. When Landmark Tower opened in 1993, its 296 m made it Japan's tallest building (until Abeno Harukas passed it in 2014). The stone dock at its foot is a Meiji-era dry dock, now home to the 1930 training sailing ship Nippon Maru. The great Ferris wheel was born at the 1989 Yokohama Expo and moved to its current site in 1999; the Red Brick Warehouses are Taisho-era customs sheds reborn in 2002 as shops and event space. One waterfront walk strings Yokohama's whole port history into a half-day stroll.
yokohama.now: 【Play】Start with Cosmo Clock 21 (¥1,000, about 15 minutes per rotation) for the harbour from 112.5 m up, then board the Nippon Maru (combo ticket with the Yokohama Port Museum ¥800), and finish on the grass deck of Osanbashi Pier at sunset. Landmark Tower's 69F Sky Garden is currently closed for the tower's renovation (reopening planned for 2028 or later), so for now admire the tower from the water's edge. 【Eat】Restaurants cluster in Landmark Plaza and Queen's Square; the Red Brick Warehouse has Yokohama Western-style classics and beer restaurants, and World Porters has a big food floor. 【Shop】Handmade goods at the Red Brick Warehouse and brands at Queen's Square; nearby, the Cup Noodles Museum lets you make your own cup noodles.
yokohama.desc: A harbour new town 30 km south of Tokyo: the 296 m Landmark Tower steps up beside the port, the 1930 sailing ship Nippon Maru rests at its foot, the 100 m Cosmo Clock 21 turns across the inlet, and the 1911 Red Brick Warehouses stand to the south. The whole bayfront lights up at night.
details: Landmark Tower & the Sky Garden (currently closed)

The tower is 296 m and 70 floors, opened in 1993; its elevators ran at 45 km/h, then the fastest in the world. The 69F Sky Garden, 273 m up, looks out to Tokyo Skytree and Mt. Fuji on clear days; admission was ¥1,000 for adults. Please note: for the tower's large-scale renovation, the Sky Garden ended operation on 31 Dec 2025 and is closed, with reopening planned for 2028 or later. Until then, visit the free Dockyard Garden and Nippon Maru at the tower's foot, and photograph the tower from the harbour side.
Cosmo Clock 21 Ferris wheel

Cosmo World charges no entry fee — you pay per ride. Its signature wheel is 100 m across and 112.5 m tall, with 60 gondolas taking about 15 minutes per rotation for ¥1,000 (the four see-through gondolas cost the same). The wheel is itself a giant clock — the world's largest when it debuted in 1989 — and at night the whole rim lights up with LED shows, the star of the Minato Mirai skyline. The park has around 30 attractions, including the 'Vanish' coaster that dives toward the water.
Red Brick Warehouse & the waterfront walk

Warehouse No. 2 was built in 1911 and No. 1 in 1913 as customs sheds for the Port of Yokohama. Today No. 2 holds shops and restaurants (mostly 11:00–20:00) and No. 1 is an exhibition and event hall; entry is free, and the plaza between them hosts markets and seasonal events. A good walking route: start at Sakuragicho Station, cross the Kishamichi promenade to the Nippon Maru and Landmark Tower, follow the inlet past Cosmo World to the Red Brick Warehouse, and end with sunset at Osanbashi Pier — flat and easy, about half a day.

yanaka.facts: About 170 m long · Some 60 small shops · Sunset steps · Famous cat street
yanaka.hist: Yanaka and its neighbours Nezu and Sendagi — 'Yanesen' for short — are among the few Tokyo districts to survive both the 1923 earthquake fires and the wartime air raids with their old townscape intact. Yanaka has been a temple town since the Edo period, and the shopping street grew after the war as the neighbourhood's everyday market: butchers, greengrocers, deli counters, senbei shops and sundries, shoulder to shoulder. The steps at the east end face due west into the sunset — hence 'Yuyake Dandan', the Sunset Steps. And Yanaka is Tokyo's cat street: pet cats, shop cats and cat-goods stores have quietly made the whole street their territory.
yanaka.now: 【Eat】Start with the menchi-katsu duel: Niku no Sato's Yanaka Menchi (¥250) against Niku no Suzuki's Ganso Genki Menchi-katsu (¥280), both fried to order and eaten at the storefront. For sweets, a cat-tail donut at Yanaka Shippoya (from ¥150), and in summer a shaved ice at Himitsudo. 【Play】Claim a spot on the Yuyake Dandan steps for sunset; in spring, walk 10 minutes to Nezu Shrine for the azaleas (April festival; azalea-garden donation ¥500–1,000), and Yanaka Cemetery's cherry avenue is nearby. 【Shop】Cat goods, hand-baked senbei and old-school deli foods — shitamachi flavours you can carry home.
yanaka.desc: An old Tokyo townscape that escaped the fires of war: some 60 small shops along a 170 m street, the 'Yuyake Dandan' sunset steps at its east end, and temples and cats across Yanesen to the west. Walk down the steps, then graze on menchi-katsu as you stroll.
details: Yuyake Dandan & the shopping street

Five minutes from JR Nippori Station's west exit, climb the steps and turn around: the street's sign arch and 170 m of shops run straight west, and at dusk the whole street turns gold — that is how the 'Sunset Steps' got their name. Cats often nap on the steps, so watch your feet. Down the steps and through the arch is the shopping street: around 60 shops, mostly serving locals at local prices. Come after 4 pm, watch the sunset first, then work your way along the shops and leave from Sendagi Station on the Chiyoda Line — a stroll with no backtracking.
The menchi-katsu duel & snack map

Yanaka Ginza's headline act is always the two butchers. Just below the steps, Niku no Sato sells the 'Yanaka Menchi' (¥250; domestic beef-and-pork mince, the juicy one); mid-street, Niku no Suzuki (founded 1933) sells the 'Ganso Genki Menchi-katsu' (¥280; bigger, bolder seasoning). The standard play is one of each, eaten hot at the storefront before you walk on — in Japanese shopping streets you don't eat while walking. For dessert, a cat-tail donut at Yanaka Shippoya (from ¥150), and in summer the famously queued shaved ice at Himitsudo — avoid the noon peak.
Wider Yanesen: Nezu Shrine & Yanaka Cemetery

Ten minutes south of the street is Nezu Shrine, said to have been founded about 1,900 years ago by Yamato Takeru and moved to its present site in 1705 by Tokugawa Tsunayoshi; the main hall is a Gongen-style Important Cultural Property, and Otome Inari Shrine inside has a tunnel of small vermillion torii. Its famous season is spring: the azalea garden's roughly 100 varieties and 3,000 bushes cover the slope in April, with a ¥500–1,000 garden donation during the Bunkyo Azalea Festival (varies with the bloom); the shrine grounds themselves are free. In the other direction, Yanaka Cemetery holds the grave of Tokugawa Yoshinobu, the last shogun, and a cherry-tree avenue loved by locals.
